classification.difficultyReason: Use the stated diameter to obtain a right angle, calculate and split a triangle angle, then transfer the required angle using a common arc.

content.prompt: In each circle below, $AB$ is a diameter. Find $\theta$.

spec.description: Diameter AB crosses chord CD; chords AC, CB and DB retain the source topology.
spec.mathematics: Angle CBA is 65 degrees and theta is angle CDB.
spec.answerVisibility: No right-angle or derived-angle answer is shown.

answer.short:
$25^\circ$

Use the right angle on diameter $AB$, then equal angles on arc $CB$.
answer.worked:
Since $AB$ is a diameter, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$.
$$\angle CAB=180^\circ-90^\circ-65^\circ=25^\circ.$$
Angles $CAB$ and $CDB$ intercept the same arc, so
$$\theta=\angle CDB=25^\circ.$$

spec.description: Diameter AB and chords AC, AD, CB and CD; AD and CB cross.
spec.mathematics: Angle CAD is 40 degrees, angle CBA is 30 degrees, and theta is angle DCB.
spec.answerVisibility: All original givens remain visible; no calculated angle is supplied.

answer.short:
$20^\circ$

Find $\angle CAB$, subtract $40^\circ$, then use equal angles on arc $DB$.
answer.worked:
Since $AB$ is a diameter, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle CAB&=180^\circ-90^\circ-30^\circ\\\angle CAB&=60^\circ\\\angle DAB&=60^\circ-40^\circ\\\angle DAB&=20^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Angles $DAB$ and $DCB$ intercept the same arc, so
$$\theta=\angle DCB=20^\circ.$$
